correctness.rationale: The statement is the saturation set, not the full profile: C_{-infty}(a,X8)=1 iff a>=sqrt(2), transferred by Liu–Din–Li Proposition 4 from J(a,X8)=2 for 0<=a<=2, and by Proposition 2 for a>2. For any two diameter equalities on the regular-octagon ball, expose their unit-length facets f,g at x. Identical facets give ||y-z||>=2; distinct simultaneous unit facets are adjacent. D8 symmetry reduces to f(s,t)=s, g(s,t)=(s+t)/sqrt(2), so y=(u,sqrt(2)-u) with u>=sqrt(2)-1 and z=(-1,v), giving ||y-z||>=u+1>=sqrt(2). The triple x=(1,sqrt(2)-1), y=(sqrt(2)-1,1), z=(-1,sqrt(2)-1) realizes equality. Scaling y inward ensures strict admissibility at a=sqrt(2), and compactness shows necessity if J approaches 2. Independent exact eight-facet/incident-face endpoint enumeration in sanity.py confirmed the geometric lemma. a=0 must be understood by the defining paper's endpoint convention: the literal displayed strict admissibility set is empty when a=0; no claim of a nonempty defining supremum at a=0 is made by this assessment.
risks: Parameter a=0 is ambiguous if the displayed strict inequality is used literally rather than the source paper endpoint convention; C_-infinity and J suprema over empty admissible triples are not defined by that literal formula. On (0,infinity) the conclusion is unaffected.
The transfer from J to C is a cited primary theorem rather than a re-proved nonstandard lemma.
